qs.q: What is the core underlying mechanism common to all thalassemia syndromes?
o: Excess production of abnormal white blood cells
Malignant proliferation of hemoglobin-producing cell lines
An autosomal recessive disorder causing excessive destruction of RBCs

qs.e: Thalassaemias are autosomal recessive blood disorders caused by variant or missing genes that lead to excessive destruction of RBCs and anemia. They are distinct from primary white blood cell disorders or pure platelet deficiencies.

es.q: Discuss the comprehensive pathophysiology, clinical presentation, investigations, complications, and treatment modalities of the thalassemia syndromes.
es.m:
- **Introduction and definition**: Thalassemia syndromes are autosomal recessive blood disorders caused by variant or missing genes affecting how the body makes hemoglobin, resulting in excessive destruction of RBCs, fewer circulating RBCs, and anemia.
- **Alpha thalassemia genetics**: Results from changes in genes of the alpha globin component (HbA1 and HbA2) encoded on chromosome 16, where normal individuals have 4 alpha globin genes (2 on each chromosome 16).
- **Alpha thalassemia pathophysiology**: Disturbed production of alpha globin causes absent normal alpha chains, excess gamma chains (fetus/newborn) or beta chains (children/adults), soluble tetramer formation (HbH), and unstable Hei
